source.name: Xin Rong Ji
source.address: No. 501, 5F, Chinese Financial Center, 33 Jiaozi Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: This branch of an upmarket chain boasts a spacious room divided into different areas, all commanding lovely views of the Twin Towers. Some ingredients are flown in from Taizhou to ensure premium quality. Seasonal gems like live seafood from Dalian and lamb from Hulunbuir are precisely crafted to highlight their natural flavours. Do not miss the raw crab marinated in amber yellow wine if available – the red, gooey roe is soft, sticky and loaded with umami.

source.name: Yu Zhi Lan
source.address: No. 1, 24 Changfa Street, Qingyang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: This low-key private dining concept can dispense with signage. The owner-chef Lan Guijun is a local legend who raised Sichuanese cooking to the level of haute cuisine, so foodies always find their way here. The quaint rustic room is dotted with ceramic art and pottery made by the chef himself. The dishes of the elaborate, multi-course set menus depend on market availability, but you can specify food allergies when booking.

source.name: Chaimen Hui
source.address: 2F, China Overseas Uni Elite, 289 Jiaozi Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: The high-end Chaimen Hui goes for an understated luxurious vibe throughout. Creative Sichuanese fare dominates the menu, courtesy of top-notch, seasonal ingredients from around the world that highlight the natural umami and layers of flavour; many dishes can be ordered in individual portions. Their ji dou hua, or minced chicken silken tofu in amber-coloured broth, boasts velvety texture and intense umami. Private rooms available for a fee.

source.name: Co-
source.address: No. 318, 3F, Chinese Financial Center, 33 Jiaozi Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: The result of the chef's extensive travel and gastronomic experiences, the multicourse tasting menu rolls out novel recipes with seasonal ingredients. Quality produce from all over China is deftly crafted using modern techniques. Don't miss the house-made sourdough, made with 20-year-old starter (or yeast), and steeped in complex flavours. Its crispy crust contrasts nicely with the spongy crumbs. There are only five tables, so booking is a must.

source.name: Fang Xiang Jing
source.address: No. 1, Courtyard 5, China Railway Ludao Art City, 16 Majia Garden Road, Jinniu, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: Set in a delicate stone garden, this restaurant in a quaint building offers private dining rooms only. The kitchen team painstakingly and faithfully revives nostalgic Sichuanese recipes. For example, the cabbage in chicken consommé takes hours to prepare and boasts a rich, crystal clear broth with exceptional depth. Contrasting textures and a tingling sensation depict the mapo tofu with diced beef and fish snout. Delicate service adds to the experience.

source.name: Fu Rong Huang
source.address: 3F, 66-16 Guanghuacun Street, Qingyang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: Privacy is a priority here and the tables are separated by wooden slatted partitions - private rooms also available. The veteran kitchen team specialises in traditional Sichuanese dishes, many of which require painstaking execution. The sautéed pork liver with chilli is perfectly cooked with just the right amount of numbing heat. The classic cold appetiser, fu qi fei pian or sliced beef offal in chili oil, is springy, flavourful and addictive.

source.name: Hokkien Cuisine
source.address: No. 326, 3F, North Tower, Chinese Financial Center, 33 Jiaozi Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: The elegant room with full-length windows feels airy and bright. In addition to booth seats, there are alsoprivate rooms for parties. The Fujian-born kitchen team ensures the authenticity of each dish. The must-try lychee meatballs are deep-fried pork stuffed with chopped water chestnuts for crunchiness. Scallion aromas and pleasing textures depict the Quanzhou speciality, crispy tofu skin rolls with a five-spice pork filling.

source.name: Ma's Kitchen (Jinjiang)
source.address: 1 East Kangshi Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: This popular eatery in the bustling Taikoo Li area started out as a stall in Weishan in 1923. Light years from its humble beginnings, this outpost of the chain in Chengdu features a vintage hipster interior and Sichuan classics on the menu. Besides their signature duck blood curd with pork offal and sliced eel, also try the crispy fen zheng rou – pork coated in seasoned rice flour, steamed and then deep-fried. Expect to see a queue from the moment it opens.

source.name: Mi Xun Teahouse
source.address: Upper House, 81 Bitieshi Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, 610021, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: Nestling in a quiet hotel next to Daci Temple, this restaurant is an oasis of calm. The courtyard house is steeped in historical charm, while the open kitchen sports an airy feel. Hand-picked local produce is used to craft light, refined and inspired vegetarian dishes. Signatures like vegan mapo tofu with termite mushroom, and handmade dan dan spinach noodles build on classic Sichuanese flavour profiles, but reimagined with modern plating and techniques.

source.name: Silver Pot
source.address: No. 532, 5F, M6, ICP Office Building, 300 Jiaozi Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: The owner’s collection of souvenirs from her trips around the world gives this spacious dining room an endearing quirkiness. Her wanderlust also translates into her quest for quality ingredients from around the globe, to be cooked in an authentic Sichuanese style. Roast pigeon smoked with Sichuan pepper leaves is simply unmissable. Cold appetisers like lamp-shadow sliced grass carp are also well made. You can opt for half portion for some dishes.

source.address: Canton Hall, Taikoo Li, 8 Zhongshamao Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: This place, the first Louis Vuitton restaurant in China, nestles in a heritage building (1730s) complete with original brick walls, perforated wood windows and a courtyard. After stints in prestigious kitchens, the experienced chef has crafted a menu that pairs sophisticated European cuisine with Sichuanese ingredients and flavour profiles. There is a handful of à la carte dishes alongside the seasonal tasting menus.

source.name: Xu's Cuisine
source.address: No. 1, Block 8, Building & Greenwich Plaza, 1 Wangjiang Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: This is the chain’s first outpost and it’s been in business for over a decade. A tank of live fish by the entrance reminds you that river and sea fish are the name of the game here. The menu revolves around novel Sichuan dishes, with a few regional offerings. For an overview of Sichuan cuisine, try the 24-flavour-profile set menu. We also recommend the preserved meat prepared in-house, or the pond loach seared with green Sichuan pepper, depicted by crisp textures and a numbing sensation.

source.address: 1-1 Tongzilin East Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
source.excerpt: This restaurant, the chain’s flagship, showcases live river fish like long snout catfish and cavefish cooked Sichuanese style or in hot pots; the owner even bought a fish farm to ensure the quality. The signature duo hot pot broth features a spicy base made with chicken, pork bones, chillies and pickles, and a tangy base of Xinjiang and Sichuan tomatoes. A la carte and set menus offer authentic fare for everyone - from solo diners to big parties.
